messages:
Anita: Quick heads-up, nightly attn-kernel run shows a p99 spike on long-seq workload (seq=4096). baseline p99 ~ 82ms, last night jumped to ~210ms. graph in bench dashboard: /d/bench/attn-nightly
Sam: Oof. Any obvious infra changes rolled out before the run? kernel or compiler flags?
Marta: Not that I'm aware of. We did push the new selector heuristic on dedicated yesterday morning but that shouldn't affect nightly infra (it only runs on canary nodes).
Anita: I grabbed the raw run: model=xl-8q, batch dist: [1,2,4,8], kvcache enabled, continuous batching on. Attn kernel used: fused-attn-v2 for most shards.
Leo: Can you paste the harness command you used? want to reproduce locally.
Anita: Here:
```
./bench-run --suite attn_longseq --model xl-8q --seq 4096 --batches 1,2,4,8 --kv-cache --repeat 3 --collect p50,p90,p99
```
Sam: Interesting — fused-attn-v2 had a micro-optim change last week that changed warp scheduling when seq>2048. Might regress tail for small batches. Did the nightly pick up the latest runtime image?
Anita: Nightly image tag: runtime:2026-11-18-rc3 (from infra bot deploy). I didn't pin the image in the harness, so it used the system image.
InfraBot: deploy notice: runtime:2026-11-18-rc3 promoted to staging at 2026-11-18T03:12:15Z by ci/cd
Leo: Ok let's triage: hypothesis A) kernel change for long seq scheduling B) changed batch composition in the harness or benchmarking sampler C) regression in the kernel fallback path causing more scalar paths.
Marta: Quick checks: 1) compare kernel version in artifacts between good and bad run, 2) run the harness with environment variable FORCE_KERNEL=v1-vs-v2 to force selection, 3) include per-op traces (attn exec time) from perf logs.
Sam: I'll run a paired run locally forcing the old kernel. If p99 drops back -> kernel change.
Anita: Running now with FORCE_KERNEL=fused-attn-v1 (same command + env). Will post numbers.
Sam: Also check nvprof logs for warp occupancy on seq4096; the scheduling tweak could reduce occupancy when batch small.
Anita: Results: baseline run with forced v1 -> p99 88ms. With v2 -> 208ms (matches nightly). So v2 is the culprit.
Leo: Cool — that narrows it. Next: is the v2 change generally better for throughput but worse for tails with small batches? If so, we need a binary selector: use v1 for p99-critical routes.
Marta: We should add a runtime policy flag: per-route kernel preference with fallback. Also, add metric tagging so console shows p99 by kernel variant.
Sam: Short-term: revert the micro-opt or add a guard for seq>2048/batch<=4 to pick v1. Long-term: fold scheduling logic into kernel selection layer where we can evaluate at runtime.
Anita: Filed RFC follow-up: rfc/attn-kernel-selection-2026-11-18 with perf traces and paired-run numbers. I'll add a canary that forces v1 for 24h and monitor user-facing p99.
Leo: Thx. Also add unit tests in harness to compare variants automatically and fail PRs that degrade p99 by >15% for our regression suites.
Marta: I'll scope the rollout plan and update the release notes. @InfraBot can we pin nightly images used in bench runs so we get reproducible artifacts?
InfraBot: action: bench infra ticket #INF-482 created to pin nightly image metadata and attach to bench artifacts
Sam: Nice. If no objections I'll prepare a 2-line revert PR for the micro-opt and a feature flag gating schedule for v2.
Anita: SGTM. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
